answers.question: What is the mechanism for?
answers.answer: It keeps the service's single, ever-growing log file from filling the disk by closing the file from time to time, putting it aside under a dated name and starting a new one.
quotes: The service writes its log into one file, and a file that only grows fills the disk.
So the service closes the file from time to time, puts it aside under a dated name and starts a new one.

answers.question: What does it take in, and what does it keep?
answers.answer: It takes in one event, a line to be written, and keeps the size of the current file and the time that file was opened.
quotes: The mechanism keeps the size of the current file and the time it was opened.
It takes in one event, a line to be written.

answers.question: By which steps does it reach its result?
answers.answer: Before each line it checks the current file against 100 megabytes and one day; under both limits it writes the line to the current file, and over either it closes the file, renames it with the date and time of closing, opens a new file and writes the line there.
quotes: Before each line the service checks the current file against two limits, 100 megabytes and one day.
Under both limits it writes the line into the current file.
Over either limit it closes the file and renames it with the date and time of closing.
It then opens a new file and writes the line there.
answers.missing: The text announces five steps and says it explains what happens to the files put aside, but the steps it gives stop at opening a new file; the step that decides what is done with the files put aside, so that only seven of them remain, is not given.

answers.question: What does a reader see when it works, on the example the text gives?
answers.answer: The text gives no worked example; it says only that put-aside files are renamed log.<date-time> and that the logs never take more than about 800 megabytes, seven files put aside and the current one.
quotes: if over:      close the file; rename it to log.<date-time>
So the logs never take more than about 800 megabytes: seven files put aside and the current one.
